decisions.reason: “Beyond” loses the source’s image of the calamity appearing at the end of the gazes.
SOL keeps the rumble rising from the abyss in natural English.
“Roaring as one” adds a coordinated action absent from the source.
The source has the rain burst forth; “scattered the driving rain” changes that physical action.
SOL keeps the people frozen in place and staring at the sight.
The Korean evokes a god’s existence; SOL preserves that singular sense.
SOL weakens the source’s certainty and drops the emphasis on the exact name and actual form.
SOL keeps the image and effect of longing for light in pitch darkness.
SOL omits that the answers become horrifyingly clear reality and changes their direction from rushing toward them to him.
The source leaves unspecified who failed to see Song Ho take out the cylinder; SOL assigns that observation to Jin Wikyung.
SOL drops the image of the sparks adorning the sky.
SOL accurately conveys that the light could be seen from the army’s rear.
“Over time” keeps the net image and its meaning.
The omitted “people” does not change who was exhausted in context.
SOL keeps the accumulated fatigue and faltering march without the unnecessary “naturally.”
SOL preserves the misfortune and the compensating good fortune in a more direct construction.
SOL keeps the contrast in martial arts skill and Wikyung’s acknowledged leadership.
“Eyes blazed like torches” preserves the image of his burning eyes.
SOL keeps the retreating people stopping in their tracks.
SOL preserves the fear and Wikyung facing the attention turned toward him.
SOL keeps their stopped feet moving forward again.
The source says Wikyung’s voice rises in force; SOL instead makes it rise above the trembling ground.
The visible faces and their exhaustion remain intact; the implied observer fits the scene.
The omitted “then” does not change the command or its condition.
“Chains around their wrists” keeps the image without changing its meaning.
The source says they are less than a hundred zhang away; SOL changes that to only a hundred.
SOL keeps the quickened breathing and visible white breath.
SOL preserves the gritty mouths and pounding hearts without changing the comparison.
SOL keeps the point that no one retreated.
SOL drops that the horses fled because they could not overcome their fear.
“Not when” maintains the source’s continuing list of reasons no one retreated.
“Tore … from where it lay embedded” preserves the boulder’s being uprooted from the plateau.
“Overhead” and “on them” preserve the boulder blocking the rain above the group.
Splitting the sentence keeps both the cry and Wikyung’s lips parting.
“Second brother” preserves the ordinal relationship in the address.
The rain, wind, and air remain in SOL’s following sentence, so the source image is retained.
SOL keeps the silent cut through the centuries-old boulder while incorporating the preceding elements.
“And it was over” keeps the sudden finality of the flash.
“Surging” preserves the blue wave overflowing from the sword in natural English.
SOL keeps the return through the heavy rain after shaking off pursuit.
“Sighed softly” preserves the small sigh at his brother’s tone.
SOL keeps the tight chin strap and the rain no longer obscuring his vision.
“Showed no sign of slowing” naturally preserves the monsters’ undiminished momentum.
“Faith in that reason” preserves his belief in why he must fight.
“We all do” naturally retains the shared belief expressed in the source.
The source calls his absence fortunate; “a relief” shifts that judgment to an emotional response.
The source says the threat to Taekyung will shrink; SOL changes this to fewer monsters threatening him.
SOL omits Wikyung walking forward after stepping out of formation.
“Closed the last distance” naturally conveys that his step was the final separation.
SOL changes the stench seeping deep into his nose to simply filling it.
The Korean does not specify that the fist was bearing down on Mukyung alone; BASE retains the group reference.
“Layered over” preserves the source’s image of new light being overlaid on the Sword Force.
Removing the comma does not change the sunset image or its gentle effect.
“Drifting on a breeze” naturally preserves the flower-petal image.
SOL keeps the realization within him without the awkward “cry echoing in his heart.”
SOL preserves his recognition of whose purple Force entered the battlefield.
The comma is unnecessary; the source’s two unknowns—when he appeared and how he moved—remain.
SOL drops the scent lingering at the tip of his nose, a sensory detail present in the source.
SOL adds “still” and loses the source’s image of a deeply lowered gaze.
“Sect Leaders” preserves the source’s specific title for the Nine Sects and One Gang’s leaders.
